# Styling inside components

Every visual value comes from a token, through a theme utility or a `ds-*` helper; every flourish on a practical component must be switchable off by `data-ds-expression="practical"`. Not for editing `tokens.css` (dooph-ds-editing-tokens) or props and API (dooph-ds-writing-components).

## Expressive details: read before any visual polish

**Test:** would a product on `data-ds-expression="practical"` expect it gone?

- **Base look:** state feedback that the spec defines, such as hover, pressed and open colours, borders, the focus ring and the disabled fade. Build it with utilities and helpers.
- **Expressive detail:** anything beyond that on a practical component (SearchBox, TextLink, a trigger, an input), such as a lean, tilt, nudge, decoration or shape. A request that says "like the caret does", "our X" or "signature" also means one.
- **Unsure:** ask the maintainer.

Expressive *components* (OutlineButton, CTAButton, shapes) are opt-in by use and are never switched.

To build an expressive detail, copy DropdownCaret's mechanism:

1. Give the detail one token, marked `/* expression */`, with a neutral value in the practical preset. dooph-ds-editing-tokens covers the steps.
2. Read the token only in a `.ds-expr-<detail>` rule in `src/styles/index.css`. Any state goes in that rule's selector.
3. The component only adds the class. It never sets the token: no inline style, arbitrary-property class, `setProperty` or prop.
4. At the neutral value, the component must still be complete, with no empty frame or gap.
5. Add a header-contract line ("must stay neutralisable by the practical preset") and a Practical story.

This applies even when the file has no header. Lint checks only tokens that are already marked, so a hard-wired utility passes it. For the full recipe and a sketch, see [references/expressive-details.md](references/expressive-details.md).

## Rules: the rule, the failure it prevents, "the lint check"

- **Colour, radius and shadow come from theme utilities** (`bg-secondary`, `rounded-tight`, `shadow-menu`). A hex or a Tailwind default ignores dark mode and overrides. "hex colour literals in components and stories", "dark-mode rules or hex colours outside tokens.css", "Tailwind default radii and shadows".
- **Spacing uses the scale words.** An off-scale value gets a token, not a bracket, because a bracket ignores token changes. "numeric Tailwind spacing", "arbitrary px/rem/em/deg in classNames". Lint knows only those units, but any bracketed look value is a missing token.
- **A token with no theme utility goes behind a `ds-*` helper**, never `[var(--ui-…)]` or `(--ui-…)`. "raw var(--ui-*) in className brackets or (--ui-*) shorthand". Where a theme utility exists, use it, always on a root that takes `className`: cn() cannot merge a helper (`cn("ds-p-ui-sm", "p-lg")` keeps both), so a consumer's class could not replace it.
- **Motion comes from the scale**, through `ds-motion-*` or `var(--ui-motion-*)` in CSS. A literal drifts from every other animation and escapes the reduced-motion collapse. Write your own reduce rule only where that collapse isn't enough: for an off-scale value (a loop, the shape-morph spring), or for motion that must become a static frame, not a shorter one (RollHover). "motion timing literals outside tokens.css", "JS timers and animation loops outside their allowlist".
- **Focus and disabled looks come from the helpers.** Hand-rolled ones drift, and they double-fade nested controls. "hand-rolled focus rings", "hand-rolled disabled looks".
- **Variants go through cva, with `className` last in `cn(…)`**, so the consumer's class wins. cn() learns class names from generated lists. After adding a `.text-style-*` or `.h-*`/`.size-*`/`.min-w-*` … rule, run `npm run sync-tokens`. Otherwise cn() misfiles the class and can erase a role as a colour. "generated theme out of date".
- **Never put a Tailwind variant on a package class** (`hover:ds-*`). It emits no rule. Put the state in the helper's selector. "Tailwind variant on a DS package class".
- **Never put `var()` in an SVG geometry attribute (`width`, `r`, `cx`…).** SVG 2 parses a presentation attribute as a value, not a declaration, so `var()` there is not specified. Chromium draws it, but its SVG DOM reads the length as 0 (`circle.r.baseVal.value`). Keep a plain number attribute and set the token through `style` or a class. `fill` and `stroke` may take `var()`. "var() in SVG geometry attributes".
- **CSS goes in `src/styles/`**, with helpers in `@layer utilities`. A `.css` under `src/components` never ships, because emit-css compiles only `src/styles/build.css`, which imports `index.css`. Text roles sit in `@layer components`, so a consumer's utility beats a role.
- **Text goes through Text components** (dooph-ds-writing-components). "text-style classes outside Text components".

## Quick reference

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Spacing (px) | `xxxs` 2, `xxs` 4, `xs` 6, `sm` 8, `rg` 10, `md` 12, `lg` 16, `xl` 20, `xxl` 26, `xxxl` 42 |
| Motion scale (`--ui-motion-*`) | `fast`, `base`, `slow`, `slower`, `slowest`; eases `standard`, `enter`, `exit`, `linear` |
| Transitions | `ds-motion-state` (colours, `rotate`, `scale`, `translate`); `ds-motion-overlay(-dialog/-sheet)` |
| Focus | `ds-focus-visible-ring`, `ds-focus-within-ring(-danger)`, `ds-focus-ring-on-focus`, `ds-focus-ring-danger-on-focus`, `ds-focus-ring-on-open`, `ds-focus-ring-sm`, `ds-shape-button-focus-visible` |
| Disabled | `ds-disabled-state`, `ds-radix-data-disabled`, `ds-opacity-disabled` (content only) |
| Tokens | [token-contract.md](../../../skills/dooph-design-system-theming/references/token-contract.md) |
| Utilities | the generated `@theme inline` block in `src/styles/index.css`: `--color-x` → `bg-x`/`text-x`, `--spacing-x` → `p-x`/`gap-x`, `--radius-x` → `rounded-x`, `--shadow-x` → `shadow-x` |

## Rationalizations

| Said in baseline | Reality |
|---|---|
| "a simple CSS rotation on hover would be more appropriate" | Simple is the bug: no preset can remove a utility. |
| "The simplest approach: add `underline decoration-wavy` Tailwind classes to TextLink." | Same bug. "Our X" exists: find it, or ask. |
| "No contract header." | The rule applies across the repo. |
| "The effect mirrors the dropdown caret's hover lean" | It copied the look, not the token or the `.ds-expr-*` rule. |

**Red flags** on a practical component:
- `hover:` or `group-hover:` combined with `rotate-`, `translate-` or `scale-`;
- `underline` or `decoration-`;
- a bracketed value.

## Verify

Run `npm run lint`. It must exit 0, and `tsc` passing on its own is not "clean". In Storybook (`npm run storybook`), check every variant and state in both themes, then check the Practical story for any trace of the detail.

## Related

# Expressive details: the full recipe

Read SKILL.md first. This file walks through DropdownCaret, the only component that ships expressive details (two of them), and then sketches the same mechanism for a new detail.

## Is it an expressive detail?

Ask: *would a product that sets `data-ds-expression="practical"` on `<html>` expect this to be gone?* If yes, it is an expressive detail. Typical cases are a hover lean, tilt or nudge, a decorative shape behind an icon, and an always-on decoration such as a wavy underline, all on a component people use for its function. A static detail counts as much as a moving one.

If it is a detail, a utility in the component's className is never the answer. The practical preset sets only custom properties, so it can't reach a hard-wired utility.

If the request names "our X", X exists somewhere in the DS. Search `src/` for it and reuse its geometry and tokens. If nothing matches, ask what X is instead of inventing it.

## The precedent: DropdownCaret

DropdownCaret has two details, its shape and its hover nudge.

**1. Tokens.** They live in `src/styles/tokens.css`, in the expression `:root` block inside `@layer ds.tokens`, each with the marker:

```css
:root {
  --ui-caret-shape-scale: 1; /* expression */
  --ui-caret-nudge: var(--ui-shape-morph-nudge); /* expression */
}
```

The practical preset in `@layer ds.expression` gives each one its neutral value:

```css
[data-ds-expression="practical"] {
  --ui-caret-shape-scale: 0;
  --ui-caret-nudge: 0;
}
```

The block is `:root` only, not `:root, .light`, so that a theme-class subtree cannot quietly bring back a detail the preset turned off. A consumer's own unlayered tokens still beat both blocks. Adding, marking and syncing a token is covered by dooph-ds-editing-tokens.

**2. Helper rules.** They sit in `src/styles/index.css`, inside `@layer utilities` and beside the component's other rules. Every read of a token happens in a `.ds-expr-*` rule:

- `.ds-expr-caret-shape` multiplies geometry by the scale. At 1 the root is a square the height of the trigger, and at 0 it is the chevron plus a trailing inset. The frame is sized by `scale × frame`, so at 0 it draws nothing and leaves no empty box. The chevron's colour is mixed by the scale, so at 0 it takes the trigger's text colour.
- `.ds-expr-caret-nudge` bridges the token into the morph engine's private input. The hover and disabled conditions live in the selector, not in a Tailwind variant:

```css
.ds-dropdown-caret-host:hover:not(:disabled):not([aria-disabled="true"]):not([data-disabled])
  .ds-expr-caret-nudge {
  --ds-shape-morph-nudge: var(--ui-caret-nudge);
}
```

**3. Component.** `DropdownCaret.tsx` adds the classes and nothing more: `"ds-dropdown-caret ds-expr-caret-shape ds-expr-caret-nudge …"`. It has no inline style, no prop and no listener for either detail. Its state comes from the nearest `.ds-dropdown-caret-host` ancestor.

**4. Header contract.** The behaviour section names both details, their tokens, their helpers and what the practical preset leaves behind. The constraints section says why: "The shape and the nudge must stay neutralisable by the practical preset", and it names the failures this prevents, a practical product still showing the signature shape, or an empty frame beside the chevron.

**5. Story.** `Practical` in `DropdownCaret.stories.tsx` renders the same triggers twice: once plain, and once inside `<div data-ds-expression="practical">`, labelled "Default (signature)" and "Practical".

## Designing the token

- Choose a value whose neutral form switches the detail off cleanly. Both caret tokens are neutral at `0`. One is a magnitude (the nudge is a lean of 0). The other is a 0–1 scale that the helper multiplies into sizes and colour mixes, so values in between interpolate.
- Write the helper so that the neutral value leaves a finished component. Work out the geometry at neutral, just as `.ds-expr-caret-shape` works out the width the chevron needs at 0.
- Take any value or angle from the spec or the maintainer. Never guess a design value, and never fall back to a bracket utility.
- Take motion from the scale. `ds-motion-state` on the moving element already transitions `rotate`, `scale`, `translate` and `transform` at `--ui-motion-duration-fast`. The caret's lean is eased by the morph engine's own rule, also on the scale, with the `base` duration and the `enter` curve. Reduced motion needs nothing extra, because the global block collapses the scale.

## Sketch: a hover lean on a practical component's icon

Every name below is **hypothetical**, and the angle is a placeholder for the spec value. The sketch shows where each piece goes.

```css
/* tokens.css, expression :root block (steps: dooph-ds-editing-tokens) */
--ui-searchbox-icon-lean: <angle from the spec>; /* expression */
/* tokens.css, [data-ds-expression="practical"] */
--ui-searchbox-icon-lean: 0deg;

/* index.css, @layer utilities: the token's only reader; state in the selector */
.ds-searchbox-host:not([data-disabled]):hover .ds-expr-searchbox-icon-lean {
  rotate: var(--ui-searchbox-icon-lean);
}
```

```tsx
// SearchBox.tsx: classes only, with no token, style or handler
<div className={cn("ds-searchbox-host …", className)}>
  <SearchIcon className="shrink-0 text-text-tertiary ds-motion-state ds-expr-searchbox-icon-lean" />
```

Then add the header-contract lines to the component and a `Practical` story built like the caret's.

## Checklist

- [ ] One token per detail, marked `/* expression */`, with its neutral value in the preset (dooph-ds-editing-tokens).
- [ ] Only `.ds-expr-*` rules read the token, and any state is in the rule's selector.
- [ ] The component adds classes only. Lint check: "expression tokens set or read outside the expression system".
- [ ] Neutralised, the component is complete, with no empty frame or gap.
- [ ] The header contract has a behaviour line and a "must stay neutralisable by the practical preset" constraint.
- [ ] A `Practical` story shows the default beside a `data-ds-expression="practical"` wrapper.
- [ ] The JSDoc describes the new default look.
- [ ] `npm run lint` exits 0. In the Practical story, the practical column shows no trace of the detail.

But the user is asking for a tilt on hover, not a shape morph or animation of the shape itself. A tilt (rotation) on hover is different from animating the shape's form. Let me re-read the constraint more carefully:

"The shape is chosen by `size`, never by a prop and never animated."

"never animated" — this says the shape is never animated. A hover tilt would animate the shape (rotate it).
